description: We are a team of programmers from IT Park University in Uzbekistan, and we aspire to build something innovative that can contribute to NASA’s mission and advance humanity’s exploration of space. Our goal is to develop a solution that pushes the boundaries of technology, addresses real-world challenges in space exploration, and helps create a better future for all humankind.
summary: The IT_Park_University team faced a major challenge; in overcoming it, we were able to develop a simulation-based game for NASA flight missions, drawing on NASA data and the practical application of GMAT. In this game, players take on the role of mission directors who oversee the entire course of events; they must also operate within specific engineering constraints, including mass limits (dry mass and fuel mass), requirements for characteristic velocity (Delta-v), power system parameters (such as solar arrays), and strict budgetary limits. As mentioned above, the game itself is built using GMAT and incorporates real NASA data. Any action taken by the player can lead to unexpected events. The core objective of our project is to make real-world NASA space missions accessible and easy to understand, helping students and others interested in the field to further their development in this area.
details: Our project is a web-based simulator that allows users to design their own spacecraft using data provided by NASA. It is built upon the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation and incorporates research and findings from NASA. The project is developed using TypeScript, React, and Tailwind CSS, with Tone.js integrated for sound. The design features a dark color palette, reminiscent of mission control systems. Every component of the spacecraft is intrinsically linked, meaning that every design choice carries specific consequences for instance, installing larger solar panels can resolve energy shortages, but it also increases the craft's overall mass.
